# Reproducible and Open Science {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[Hands-on lessons for computational biologists: organize, record, rerun and
share an analysis.]{.lead}

[Set up your computer](pages/00-setup.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Browse the lessons](contents.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
[7-week schedule](schedule-course.qmd){.btn .btn-link}
:::

Your analysis worked last month. Can you rerun it today? Can a reviewer, a
labmate, or you in five years? This workshop teaches the tools and habits that
make the answer *yes*: project organization, data management, literate
programming with Quarto and Jupyter, version control with Git and GitHub,
software environments with Pixi, containers, workflow managers (Snakemake and
Nextflow), documentation, and open publication.

Everything is hands-on and built around **one project** that grows with you:
variant calling on *E. coli* from Richard Lenski's
[Long-Term Evolution Experiment](pages/ltee-project.qmd). You do not need to
know genomics: the analysis is a given pipeline, and the lessons are about
making it reproducible.

## What you will be able to do

- Start a project with a clear layout, download its data with checksums, and keep raw data untouched
- Write reports in which every number and figure is computed from the data
- Track your work with Git, collaborate through pull requests, and let GitHub rerun it on every push
- Pin your software with Pixi lock files, and ship it in containers
- Run a multi-step pipeline with Snakemake and Nextflow, and get identical results from both
- Document, license, cite and archive your work with a DOI

## Built on open material

This course began as a [mini-course at Stanford Biosciences](https://explorecourses.stanford.edu/search?q=BIOS+259&view=catalog&page=0&filter-coursestatus-Active=on&collapse=&academicYear=20232024)
([BIOS259, Winter 2024](https://github.com/asntech/bios259-w24/)), developed by Aziz Khan and taught with the help of
Alvina, Clemens and Brennan.

The material adapts and extends open lessons from [NBIS](https://nbisweden.github.io/), 
[The carpentry](https://software-carpentry.org), [The Data Carpentry](https://datacarpentry.org/) and many more. See [Sources and credits](pages/credits.qmd).
